memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Visit for obesity management.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports gradual weight gain over the past year, feeling heaviness and mild knee discomfort on walking.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 82 kg, height 1.58 m => BMI 32.8 (obese). Waist circumference 102 cm. General appearance well‑nourished, no distress. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams normal.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI class II. No overt metabolic syndrome yet; plan to check fasting lipid profile and glucose.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start orlistat 120 mg with each main meal. Advise reduced‑calorie diet and increase walking to 30 minutes daily. Return if new joint pain, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or fever >39°C. Influenza vaccine not due yet (outside autumn). Asked patient to repeat the return‑if list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Orlistat 120 mg PO TID with breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Continue for 12 weeks, review then.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been taking the orlistat with meals as prescribed. Over the past two weeks I’ve noticed oily spotting after fatty meals and occasional mild abdominal cramping, but no vomiting or severe pain. My weight hasn’t changed much yet; I’m still around 82 kg. I’ve tried to walk a bit more but my knee feels sore after longer walks.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up on obesity and orlistat tolerance.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports oily stools and mild cramping after fatty meals, otherwise stable weight.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 81.5 kg, height 1.58 m => BMI 32.6 (obese). Waist 101 cm. Abdomen soft, no tenderness. No signs of dehydration.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI class II. Orlistat associated gastrointestinal side effects expected; lipid panel shows modest improvement.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue orlistat 120 mg TID with meals. Advise low‑fat diet to reduce oily spotting, maintain walking 20‑30 min daily as tolerated. Return if severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, signs of electrolyte loss, or fever >39°C. Influenza vaccine not yet due. Asked patient to repeat return‑if list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine obesity review; influenza vaccine discussion.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient stable, reports mild oily spotting only after high‑fat meals, weight unchanged.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 81.0 kg, height 1.58 m => BMI 32.4 (obese). Waist 100 cm. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams normal.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI class II. Lipids now within target; glucose and HbA1c normal. Orlistat tolerated.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue orlistat 120 mg TID with meals. Give inactivated influenza vaccine today (01‑Nov‑2025). Advise balanced diet, aim for 150 min weekly walking. Return if new chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or gastrointestinal bleeding. Asked patient to repeat return‑if list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Weight check and lifestyle review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient notes gradual weight increase of about 1.5 kg over last 4 months, feeling more fatigued.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 82.5 kg, height 1.58 m => BMI 33.0 (obese). Waist 102 cm. No edema, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: Obesity, BMI class II. Weight regain likely due to dietary lapses; labs remain stable.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reinforce orlistat 120 mg TID with meals, strict low‑fat diet, increase activity to brisk walking 30‑40 min daily. Consider reviewing diet with nutritionist if no improvement in 2 months. Return if new joint swelling, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or fever >39°C. Influenza vaccine not due (outside autumn). Asked patient to repeat return‑if list.
